focus.rationale: T13 re-derivation (2026-09-10, permissive reading, §10.2.1): smoothing_route is cationic_alignment on a two-observation SFR-high read (film: Guar Hydroxypropyltrimonium Chloride r5; lubrication: Dicaprylyl Ether r4), clearing §7.4.1's two-observation test. COND high was over-satisfied (the LGN pair r2/r7/r8 alone would have carried it), so under the conservative reading the film route read as baseline conditioning; under the now-adopted permissive reading, a single admissible establishing set (the LGN pair) suffices to leave the cationic film beyond baseline. No qualifying repair route exists (R2 none_visible, and the marketing-position prong is deleted by T13a; claims[] is empty in any case), so repair is unavailable and does not out-rank smoothing. Every other route fails its own gate (curl_definition: HOLD none; heat_styling: HEAT not_claimed; detangling: no C1/C2 positioning and COND/WT both too high; volume_lightness: WT high; shine: would restate the smoothing film, G3). Supersedes this record's pre-T13 focus_basis (there was none recorded; the v3 evidence chain's Focus section states the conservative-reading `general` result and predates this ruling).
focus.derivation: §10.2: qualifying routes are collected beyond baseline conditioning (§10.2.1, permissive reading T13b), then the rank order repair > smoothing > curl_definition > heat_styling > detangling > volume_lightness > shine binds.
thresholdReasoning: Selected primary `smoothing` with secondary [].
§10.2 principle 4: official positioning may corroborate a route but never creates one.
limitations: A focus is a statement of distinctive purpose, not an efficacy claim or a measured endpoint.

limitations: A route type, not a smoothing score; it carries no humidity or frizz claim (§7.9).
